> [@grimdalltech](https://github.com/grimdalltech) appreciate the engagement, but do you actually provide a sandbox? Or just something to use in combination with a sandbox? Then, this might not be the correct issue for you here...

fair question — let me clarify the distinction:
Grimdall is not a sandbox. it's a policy enforcer that sits at the tool-call boundary (AST-parses shell commands, blocks destructive ops, denies secret reads, enforces spend caps, signs receipts). it's complementary to OS-level sandboxes (Docker, Firecracker, Bubblewrap), not a replacement.
the reason I commented: sandboxes restrict what the kernel allows, but they don't stop an agent with legitimate shell access from rm -rf /workspace or reading ssh/id_rsa if the sandbox permits it. that's the "confused deputy" problem — the agent holds valid credentials by design, so enforcement has to happen below the model, at the policy layer.
if this issue is specifically about OS-level sandboxing and not policy enforcement, then yes — this might not be the right thread. happy to step back if it's off-topic. 🫡

Reproducing on v1.18.23 with a different symptom than @nico2525nn's follow-up describes — direct URL navigation **does NOT load the requested session's messages**, even though the server-side API has them.

**Repro:**
1. Have a session `ses_A` (e.g. created via `POST /api/session` + a prompt) on a server at `http://100.97.238.38:4096`. Server detail endpoint returns it fine: `GET /api/session/ses_A` → 200 with `data.location.directory = "/Users/.../dev"`.
2. In a fresh browser context (or one where `http://100.97.238.38:4096` is in localStorage as a known server with at least one project added), open the direct URL the UI itself generates when navigating from the sidebar:
   `http://100.97.238.38:4096/server/{base64("http://100.97.238.38:4096")}/session/ses_A`
3. UI boots, route matches `/server/:key/session/:id`, then the URL bar changes to `/server/{...}/session/ses_B` where `ses_B` is some other session (in my case `ses_fc2934cc1ffeEHx0xfH0t04ZhI` — title "New session - 2026-08-26T09:35:29.091Z", created 2026-08-26T09:35:29, also `directory=/Users/.../dev`). The main area shows the empty "New session" editor; no `/api/session/ses_A/message` request is made.

**Expected:** UI loads `ses_A` and renders its messages.
**Actual:** UI redirects to a different session ID and shows an empty editor. The requested session's messages are never fetched.

**Differs from @nico2525nn's follow-up:** they reported "the session itself still loads, since sessions come from the server DB" — i.e. only the sidebar/projects list was broken on URL navigation. In my repro the session itself is also dropped and replaced with a different one. Possibly version-specific (mine 1.18.23 vs theirs 0.0.0-beta-17728).

Workaround I'm shipping for my dashboard: a custom modal session viewer that proxies `GET /api/session/{id}` and `GET /api/session/{id}/message` and renders the timeline inline. Would prefer to drop it once this is fixed.

The duplicate check — this overlaps with #25096, #32776, #40885, #22623 on symptom (all are `max_tokens` vs `max_completion_tokens`), but those are scoped to specific providers/model families (Azure, cloudflare-ai-gateway, gpt-5.x by name). This report is about the general case: any `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider pointed at a gateway that requires `max_completion_tokens`, regardless of model name or which gateway it is. Happy to have this closed in favor of one of those if maintainers prefer to track it there instead.

Dug into this a bit more before proposing a fix, since I initially assumed there was one request path — there are actually two:

- **Native runtime** (`packages/llm`, opt-in via `experimentalNativeLlm`) — not the default, most users won't hit this.
- **AI SDK runtime** (default) — calls `streamText()` from Vercel's `ai` package, which builds the request via `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` directly. This is the path everyone in the linked issues is actually hitting, and it always sends `max_tokens` with no way to configure otherwise.

Two things ruled out:
- A blanket rewrite to `max_completion_tokens` for all `openai-compatible` providers — unsafe, since plenty of self-hosted OpenAI-compatible servers only accept `max_tokens` and would break.
- Matching on model name (e.g. `gpt-5*`) — works today but is brittle for future model families and doesn't help custom-named providers behind a gateway (like this report).

**Proposed fix:** an explicit, opt-in compatibility flag on the model config, e.g.

```jsonc
"models": {
  "gpt-5.4": {
    "compatibility": { "maxTokensField": "max_completion_tokens" }
  }
}
```

honored by the default request-prep path before `streamText` is called. This isn't a new concept — `packages/llm/src/schema/options.ts` already has `ModelCompatibility` with a `toolSchema` field for this exact kind of "known upstream quirk," just currently scoped to the native runtime only. This would widen that pattern to the default path and add the token-field case.

Implementation-wise, this doesn't need new plugin API either — @ai-sdk/openai-compatible already lets provider options pass through for any key it doesn't recognize as standard, which is the same mechanism the existing Cerebras/Snowflake Cortex plugins use to do this rewrite today. This would just be that same technique, driven by the config flag instead of a hardcoded provider check.

Additional repro detail (v1.18.23): navigating via the sidebar session list **does** render messages correctly, but only the direct URL navigation breaks.

Steps:
1. Open `http://100.97.238.38:4096/` → UI boots, redirects to `/server/{key}/session/ses_X`. Sidebar shows session list fine. But main area is **empty** (just the "New session" editor, no messages for `ses_X`).
2. Click on any session in the sidebar list → UI loads it correctly: messages render, scroll works, all good.
3. Copy the URL bar from step 2 (`/server/{key}/session/ses_Y`) and paste into a fresh tab → UI boots, lands on the correct route, but main area is **empty again** — no `/api/session/{id}/message` request fired.

So the URL→route matching itself seems to work (no "Invalid server route" error, no redirect to a different session), but the message-fetching effect is not triggered on direct navigation. It only fires when the route transition originates from inside the SPA (sidebar click).

Server logs show the `/api/session/{id}` (detail) request is made on both paths, but `/api/session/{id}/message` only on the sidebar-click path.

Hope that helps narrow the scope.

> This issue might be a duplicate of or closely related to existing issues. Please check:
> 
> * [Session token usage grows unbounded via cache.read and causes unrecoverable context-window errors #30649](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/30649): Session token usage grows unbounded via cache.read and causes unrecoverable context-window errors — similar symptom of compaction not triggering and cache.read tokens accumulating without bound, leading to quota/context exhaustion on long sessions.

Thanks for the auto-flag - I looked into #30649 in detail and don't think this is a duplicate.

#30649's core complaint is the lifetime cumulative `tokens_cache_read` counter on the session row looking alarmingly large, and a related false-overflow bug in `overflow.ts` for providers that return huge per-message `cache.read` values (DeepSeek/MiMo). The most recent analysis on that thread (@Zaczero) traced every reader of those session-level counters and concluded they're purely a display/stats artifact that nothing in compaction actually consults - and explicitly says a real context-window/compaction failure "is a different bug that this report may have misattributed... it deserves its own issue."

This report is that different bug: on `github-copilot`/`claude-sonnet-5`, `session_context_epoch` stays at `0` for the entire 6-day session even though the real, per-message context (not a cumulative artifact) kept growing normally turn over turn. Compaction never fired even once - the opposite failure direction from #30649's false-overflow case, on a different provider, and (per Zaczero's source trace) a different code path than the one #30649 is about.

Happy to help narrow this down further if it'd be useful.

I made a narrower version of this PR: https://github.com/AnnoyingTechnology/opencode/tree/cache-compaction

It keeps serialized compaction as the default. The opt-in replay runs only for same-model OpenAI-compatible requests at safe turn boundaries; every unsupported case falls back unchanged. It preserves the triggering request identity: agent, variant, system, tool filters, and tools, while setting `toolChoice: "none"`.

The branch includes generated schema/SDK updates, exact wire-prefix tests, and fallback tests. 

If you agree with this scope, please use or cherry-pick commit `e41db562e` into this PR. Keeping your PR and **narrowing it should improve its merge chances**: the feature remains available, while default behavior and unsupported providers remain untouched.

Seeing the identical warning on Windows 11, opencode v1.18.23 (npm global install), Node v24.18.0:

```
MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventTarget memory leak detected.
11 event listeners added
    at overflowWarning (node:events)
    at addListener (node:events)
    at ~effect/Effect/evaluate
    at runLoop
    at evaluate
```

Same "11 event listeners" count as the original report, on a different OS/Node version — suggests the count isn't strongly driven by plugin load, since I have 2 plugins active (`oh-my-opencode-slim` + `@opengsd/gsd-core`) totaling ~9 registered hook keys, and I could not reproduce it via `opencode serve` + session creation + SSE `/event` subscription in isolation — it seems to require a fuller interactive session/chat-turn lifecycle to trip. Ruled out plugin duplication as the cause on my end (confirmed via `opencode debug config` → `plugin_origins`, no duplicate registrations). Happy to provide more diagnostics if useful.

Can confirm this is still present (reproduced 2026-08-26).

The root cause analysis in the issue description matches what I found independently. One update: in the current tree the file has moved to `packages/tui/src/routes/session/permission.tsx` (the repo was restructured — `tui` is now its own top-level package rather than living under `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui`). `EditBody` there reads only `request.metadata.diff` and feeds the whole string into a single `<diff>` renderer, which only displays the first file when `apply_patch` concatenates every changed file's patch into that one string via `totalDiff`. `request.metadata.files` (already populated per-file in `apply_patch.ts`, with `relativePath`/`patch`/`type` per entry) has everything needed to fix this — it's just not consumed by the permission view.

For what it's worth: I maintain a JetBrains IDE plugin that also renders this permission diff live (outside the TUI), and switching it from `metadata.diff` to iterating `metadata.files` fixed the identical symptom with no other changes needed — so iterating `metadata.files` when present does look like the correct, minimal fix here too.
